newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Congress censures lawmaker in sex case.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Congress censures lawmaker in sex case.

text.p: The Philippine House of Representatives on Tuesday voted to censure a lawmaker charged with the statutory rape of an 11-year-old girl after throwing out a panel's recommendation to suspend him from office.
The house, on a vote of 76-46, approved a resolution reducing the administrative penalty to be imposed on congressman Romeo Jalosjos from suspension to mere censure.

Jalosjos, a member of President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition in the chamber, is charged in court with statutory rape and acts of lasciviousness for having sex with the girl in his Manila apartment last year.
The congressman, who denies the charges, was on the run for more than three weeks until he was arrested on a small island near Manila on January 17. The cases are pending in court.

The congressional ethics committee recommended that Jalosjos be suspended in a resolution in January. But the entire house amended the resolution and reduced the penalty to censure after realising it would not get the two-thirds vote required to suspend a member, congressional sources said.
